Iridaceae ( / ɪ r ɪ ˈ d eɪ s i ˌ aɪ , - s iː ˌ iː / ) is a family of plants in order Asparagales , taking its name from the irises . It has a nearly global distribution, with 69 accepted genera with a total of about 2500 species. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] It includes a number of economically important cultivated plants, such as species of Freesia , Gladiolus , and Crocus , as well as the crop saffron .
